target.near: "The lamp as we have built it is a process of our thinking, and it cannot be changed without changing our thinking."

provenance: M38, rung 3. Deployment run e6768ee0: `{near: "“The world as we have created it …”"}` ended `failure:locate — no tier resolved`, with the answer one element away from the anchor. Two things break an anchor string that came back through a model: the page renders typographic quotes (U+201C/U+201D) and the plan quotes them back as ASCII (or the reverse), and the plan reproduces MORE of the sentence than the page shows. `get_by_text` is a literal substring match, so both are total misses, and a miss on the anchor is indistinguishable from 'this page does not have it'. The `near` string here does both at once: straight quotes against the fixture's typographic ones, and a sentence the page truncates at 'thinking.' — so the case is red unless BOTH the normalising pass and the prefix fallback exist. Watched red first: `status failure:locate`, reason `element-not-found: no tier resolved {'role': 'link', 'near': '"The lamp as we have built it is a process of our thinking, and it cannot be changed without changing our thinking."'}` (relocation offered no rung either: the target has neither `name` nor `text`, so there is nothing to relocate BY).

triage.what_this_grades: that an anchor which the page contains in substance but not byte-for-byte still resolves: quote/apostrophe/dash characters match their typographic variants, runs of whitespace match each other, and a long anchor falls back to its first 40 characters. The fallback ORDER is what keeps it honest — exact, then substring, then normalised, then prefix — so the loosest match is only ever reached when every stricter one found nothing.
triage.not_covered: a prefix that is itself ambiguous. It is matched by the same NEAREST_JS rules as any other anchor, so two non-nested matches for the prefix are still a loud `ambiguous-match` rather than a guess (near-anchor-substring's ruling, one loosening further down).
